_comment: Near-duplicate pairs that have been opened and read, with the verdict.
plan.md Phase 9 §3's test is: open both, and write one sentence saying who
each is for. If the sentence is the same, one of them should not exist.
This file is where that sentence goes, so tools/near_duplicates.py can stop
reporting a pair as unread once somebody has read it.
A pair is keyed by domain and title exactly as the census prints them. A
retitle therefore invalidates the verdict, which is correct: a new title can
change the answer. near_duplicates.py reports entries whose pair no longer
scores above the floor, so this file cannot quietly rot.
Only 'keep' verdicts belong here. A pair that should be consolidated is not
recorded, it is merged - see tools/retire_topic.py.

b: TCP/IP Model — 4 Layers vs OSI Mapping
verdicts.why: Two different reference models: the seven-layer teaching model, and the four-layer one the internet actually runs — which exists to map onto it.
Different objects, same word. One cycles risks a business accepts or treats; the other cycles findings a scanner produced.
One is for choosing and operating the queue — pub/sub, delivery guarantees, idempotence. The other is for the reasoning change events force, where you trade the stack trace for a correlation ID.

b: Linux Permissions — Who Can Do What, In Depth
verdicts.why: One is the model — the bit layout, and what those bits mean on a directory, where write lets you delete a file you cannot read. The other is the job: read it, change it, and the four mechanisms that override it.

a: Progressive Web Apps (PWA) — Web Apps That Feel Native
verdicts.why: The teaching card and the caveat card: four cards introducing service workers, beside the one saying a service worker makes the browser a distributed-systems node.

a: OWASP Top 10 — The Most Critical Web Security Risks
b: The OWASP API Security Top 10 — Where the Web List Stops Being Enough
verdicts.why: Two different lists. The API list exists because the API's bugs are not the web list's, which the second card's own subtitle says.

a: OWASP Top 10 — The Most Critical Web Security Risks
verdicts.why: An explainer beside the list itself for exam recall — §3's reference row, which the census cannot see here because the card is a list without calling itself one.

a: Asset & Configuration Management — A CMDB That Stays True
verdicts.why: A name collision. One is ITIL — a CMDB that stays true, and why most are wrong. The other is Ansible — making servers match a desired state.

a: SOLID Principles — Writing Code That Survives Change
verdicts.why: The teaching card and the caveat card: five principles with a before-and-after, beside 'an interface with one implementation is a guess about the future'.

b: AWS IAM Deep — AssumeRole, STS & Boundaries
verdicts.why: The basics — who can do what, and iam:PassRole — beside the delegation layer: AssumeRole, STS, and why a permission can be granted and still denied. The level marker is in the title, not the badge, which is why §3's first row cannot see it.

b: Network Automation – Configuring Switches & Routers with Python ▶
verdicts.why: The teaching card and the caveat card: connecting with Netmiko and looping over devices, beside 'the config is not the state, and the device you lock out is the one you are standing in'.

b: Container Breakout Paths & Pod Security Standards
verdicts.why: Hardening the image beside the escape paths — what to do, and what an attacker reaches for when you did not.

a: API Design — Versioning, Pagination, Rate Limits & Idempotency
verdicts.why: The teaching card and the caveat card: versioning, pagination and rate limits, beside the contract and the three questions to ask of it.

a: OLTP vs OLAP — Transactional vs Analytical Data
b: OLTP vs OLAP — Rows vs Columns
verdicts.why: The teaching card and the caveat card: two jobs and two storage layouts, beside 'the update is the problem, not the query'.
The teaching card and the caveat card: POUR and the highest-impact habits, beside 'a clean automated scan is the floor, not the result'.
The essentials card and the caveat card: where secrets leak and what to store them in, beside 'nothing can be rotated, because rotation was never once performed'.

a: Difficult Conversations — Angry Users, VIP Pressure & Saying No
b: Feedback & Difficult Conversations — Specific, Timely & Survivable
verdicts.why: Different audiences. A service desk facing an angry user and VIP pressure, and a team lead giving feedback to a report.
